lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: we look from his age to receive not alone the imperfections of

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: long-engrafted condition, but therewithal the unruly waywardness

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: that infirm and choleric years bring with them.

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Such unconstant starts are we like to have from him as this of Kent’s

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: banishment.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: There is further compliment of leave-taking between France and

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: him. Pray you let us hit together: if our father carry authority

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: with such disposition as he bears, this last surrender of his

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: will but offend us.

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: We shall further think of it.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: We must do something, and i’ th’ heat.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A Hall in the Earl of Gloucester’s Castle

lines.text: Enter Edmund with a letter.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Thou, Nature, art my goddess; to thy law

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: My services are bound. Wherefore should I

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Stand in the plague of custom, and permit

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: The curiosity of nations to deprive me?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: For that I am some twelve or fourteen moonshines

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Lag of a brother? Why bastard? Wherefore base?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: When my dimensions are as well compact,

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: My mind as generous, and my shape as true

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: As honest madam’s issue? Why brand they us

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: With base? With baseness? bastardy? Base, base?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Who, in the lusty stealth of nature, take

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: More composition and fierce quality

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Than doth within a dull stale tired bed

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Go to the creating a whole tribe of fops

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Got ’tween asleep and wake? Well then,

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Legitimate Edgar, I must have your land:

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Our father’s love is to the bastard Edmund

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: As to the legitimate: fine word: legitimate!

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Well, my legitimate, if this letter speed,

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: And my invention thrive, Edmund the base

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Shall top the legitimate. I grow, I prosper.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Now, gods, stand up for bastards!
Enter Gloucester.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Kent banish’d thus! and France in choler parted!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And the King gone tonight! Prescrib’d his pow’r!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Confin’d to exhibition! All this done

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Upon the gad!—Edmund, how now! What news?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: So please your lordship, none.
[_Putting up the letter._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Why so earnestly seek you to put up that letter?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I know no news, my lord.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: What paper were you reading?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Nothing, my lord.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: No? What needed then that terrible dispatch of it into your pocket? The

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: quality of nothing hath not such need to hide itself. Let’s see. Come,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: if it be nothing, I shall not need spectacles.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I beseech you, sir, pardon me. It is a letter from my brother that I

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: have not all o’er-read; and for so much as I have perus’d, I find it

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: not fit for your o’er-looking.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Give me the letter, sir.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I shall offend, either to detain or give it. The contents, as in

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: part I understand them, are to blame.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Let’s see, let’s see!

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I hope, for my brother’s justification, he wrote this but as an

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: essay, or taste of my virtue.
[_Reads._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: ‘This policy and reverence of age makes the world

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: bitter to the best of our times; keeps our fortunes from us

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: till our oldness cannot relish them. I begin to find an idle

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: and fond bondage in the oppression of aged tyranny; who sways

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: not as it hath power, but as it is suffered. Come to me, that

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: of this I may speak more. If our father would sleep till I

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: waked him, you should enjoy half his revenue for ever, and live

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: the beloved of your brother EDGAR.’

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Hum! Conspiracy? ‘Sleep till I wake him, you should enjoy half

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: his revenue.’—My son Edgar! Had he a hand to write this? A heart

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: and brain to breed it in? When came this to you? Who brought it?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: It was not brought me, my lord, there’s the cunning of it. I

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: found it thrown in at the casement of my closet.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: You know the character to be your brother’s?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: If the matter were good, my lord, I durst swear it were his; but

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: in respect of that, I would fain think it were not.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: It is his.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: It is his hand, my lord; but I hope his heart is not in the

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: contents.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Has he never before sounded you in this business?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Never, my lord. But I have heard him oft maintain it to be fit

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: that, sons at perfect age, and fathers declined, the father

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: should be as ward to the son, and the son manage his revenue.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: O villain, villain! His very opinion in the letter! Abhorred

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: villain! Unnatural, detested, brutish villain! worse than

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: brutish! Go, sirrah, seek him; I’ll apprehend him. Abominable

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: villain, Where is he?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I do not well know, my lord. If it shall please you to suspend

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: your indignation against my brother till you can derive from him

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: better testimony of his intent, you should run a certain course;

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: where, if you violently proceed against him, mistaking his

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: purpose, it would make a great gap in your own honour, and shake

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: in pieces the heart of his obedience. I dare pawn down my life

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: for him, that he hath writ this to feel my affection to your

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: honour, and to no other pretence of danger.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Think you so?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: If your honour judge it meet, I will place you where you shall hear us

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: confer of this, and by an auricular assurance have your satisfaction,

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: and that without any further delay than this very evening.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: He cannot be such a monster.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Nor is not, sure.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To his father, that so tenderly and entirely loves him. Heaven

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: and earth! Edmund, seek him out; wind me into him, I pray you:

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: frame the business after your own wisdom. I would unstate myself

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: to be in a due resolution.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I will seek him, sir, presently; convey the business as I shall

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: find means, and acquaint you withal.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: These late eclipses in the sun and moon portend no good to us:

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: though the wisdom of Nature can reason it thus and thus, yet

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: nature finds itself scourged by the sequent effects. Love cools,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: friendship falls off, brothers divide: in cities, mutinies; in

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: countries, discord; in palaces, treason; and the bond cracked

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: ’twixt son and father. This villain of mine comes under the

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: prediction; there’s son against father: the King falls from

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: bias of nature; there’s father against child. We have seen the

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: best of our time. Machinations, hollowness, treachery, and all

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: ruinous disorders follow us disquietly to our graves. Find out

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: this villain, Edmund; it shall lose thee nothing; do it

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: carefully.—And the noble and true-hearted Kent banished! his

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: offence, honesty! ’Tis strange.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: This is the excellent foppery of the world, that, when we are

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: sick in fortune, often the surfeits of our own behaviour, we

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: make guilty of our disasters the sun, the moon, and the stars; as

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: if we were villains on necessity; fools by heavenly compulsion;

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: knaves, thieves, and treachers by spherical predominance;

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: drunkards, liars, and adulterers by an enforced obedience of

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: planetary influence; and all that we are evil in, by a divine

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: thrusting on. An admirable evasion of whoremaster man, to lay his

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: goatish disposition to the charge of a star. My father compounded

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: with my mother under the dragon’s tail, and my nativity was under

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Ursa Major, so that it follows I am rough and lecherous. Fut! I

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: should have been that I am, had the maidenliest star in the

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: firmament twinkled on my bastardizing.
Enter Edgar.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Pat! he comes, like the catastrophe of the old comedy: my cue

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: is villainous melancholy, with a sigh like Tom o’Bedlam.—O,

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: these eclipses do portend these divisions! Fa, sol, la, mi.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: How now, brother Edmund, what serious contemplation are you in?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I am thinking, brother, of a prediction I read this other day,

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: what should follow these eclipses.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Do you busy yourself with that?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I promise you, the effects he writes of succeed unhappily: as of

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: unnaturalness between the child and the parent; death, dearth,

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: dissolutions of ancient amities; divisions in state, menaces and

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: maledictions against King and nobles; needless diffidences,

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: banishment of friends, dissipation of cohorts, nuptial breaches,

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: and I know not what.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: How long have you been a sectary astronomical?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Come, come! when saw you my father last?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: The night gone by.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Spake you with him?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Ay, two hours together.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Parted you in good terms? Found you no displeasure in him, by word

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: nor countenance?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: None at all.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Bethink yourself wherein you may have offended him: and at my

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: entreaty forbear his presence until some little time hath

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: qualified the heat of his displeasure; which at this instant so

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: rageth in him that with the mischief of your person it would

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: scarcely allay.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Some villain hath done me wrong.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: That’s my fear. I pray you have a continent forbearance till the

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: speed of his rage goes slower; and, as I say, retire with me to

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: my lodging, from whence I will fitly bring you to hear my lord

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: speak: pray ye, go; there’s my key. If you do stir abroad, go

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: armed.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Armed, brother?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Brother, I advise you to the best; I am no honest man

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: if there be any good meaning toward you: I have told you what I

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: have seen and heard. But faintly; nothing like the image and

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: horror of it: pray you, away!

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Shall I hear from you anon?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: I do serve you in this business.
[_Exit Edgar._]

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: A credulous father! and a brother noble,

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Whose nature is so far from doing harms

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: That he suspects none; on whose foolish honesty

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: My practices ride easy! I see the business.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Let me, if not by birth, have lands by wit;

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: All with me’s meet that I can fashion fit.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: A Room in the Duke of Albany’s Palace

lines.text: Enter Goneril and Oswald.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Did my father strike my gentleman for chiding of his fool?

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: Ay, madam.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: By day and night, he wrongs me; every hour

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: He flashes into one gross crime or other,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: That sets us all at odds; I’ll not endure it:

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: His knights grow riotous, and himself upbraids us

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: On every trifle. When he returns from hunting,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: I will not speak with him; say I am sick.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: If you come slack of former services,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: You shall do well; the fault of it I’ll answer.
[_Horns within._]

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: He’s coming, madam; I hear him.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Put on what weary negligence you please,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: You and your fellows; I’d have it come to question:

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: If he distaste it, let him to our sister,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Whose mind and mine, I know, in that are one,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Not to be overruled. Idle old man,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: That still would manage those authorities

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: That he hath given away! Now, by my life,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Old fools are babes again; and must be us’d

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: With checks as flatteries, when they are seen abus’d.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Remember what I have said.

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: Very well, madam.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: And let his knights have colder looks among you;

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: What grows of it, no matter; advise your fellows so;

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: I would breed from hence occasions, and I shall,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: That I may speak. I’ll write straight to my sister

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: To hold my very course. Prepare for dinner.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Kent, disguised.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: If but as well I other accents borrow,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: That can my speech defuse, my good intent

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: May carry through itself to that full issue

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: For which I rais’d my likeness. Now, banish’d Kent,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: If thou canst serve where thou dost stand condemn’d,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: So may it come, thy master, whom thou lov’st,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Shall find thee full of labours.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Horns within. Enter King

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Lear, Knights and Attendants.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Let me not stay a jot for dinner; go get it ready.
[_Exit an Attendant._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: How now! what art thou?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: A man, sir.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What dost thou profess? What wouldst thou with us?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: I do profess to be no less than I seem; to serve him truly that

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: will put me in trust; to love him that is honest; to converse

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: with him that is wise and says little; to fear judgement; to fight

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: when I cannot choose; and to eat no fish.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What art thou?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: A very honest-hearted fellow, and as poor as the King.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: If thou be’st as poor for a subject as he’s for a king, thou art

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: poor enough. What wouldst thou?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Service.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Who wouldst thou serve?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: You.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Dost thou know me, fellow?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: No, sir; but you have that in your countenance which I would fain

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: call master.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What’s that?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Authority.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What services canst thou do?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: I can keep honest counsel, ride, run, mar a curious tale in

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: telling it and deliver a plain message bluntly. That which

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: ordinary men are fit for, I am qualified in, and the best of

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: me is diligence.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: How old art thou?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Not so young, sir, to love a woman for singing; nor so old to

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: dote on her for anything: I have years on my back forty-eight.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Follow me; thou shalt serve me. If I like thee no worse after dinner, I

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: will not part from thee yet. Dinner, ho, dinner! Where’s my knave? my

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: fool? Go you and call my fool hither.
[_Exit an Attendant._]
Enter Oswald.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: You, you, sirrah, where’s my daughter?

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: So please you,—
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What says the fellow there? Call the clotpoll back.
[_Exit a Knight._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Where’s my fool? Ho, I think the world’s asleep.
Re-enter Knight.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: How now! where’s that mongrel?

lines.speaker: KNIGHT
lines.text: He says, my lord, your daughter is not well.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Why came not the slave back to me when I called him?

lines.speaker: KNIGHT
lines.text: Sir, he answered me in the roundest manner, he would not.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: He would not?

lines.speaker: KNIGHT
lines.text: My lord, I know not what the matter is; but to my judgement your

lines.speaker: KNIGHT
lines.text: highness is not entertained with that ceremonious affection as

lines.speaker: KNIGHT
lines.text: you were wont; there’s a great abatement of kindness appears as

lines.speaker: KNIGHT
lines.text: well in the general dependants as in the Duke himself also, and

lines.speaker: KNIGHT
lines.text: your daughter.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Ha! say’st thou so?

lines.speaker: KNIGHT
lines.text: I beseech you pardon me, my lord, if I be mistaken; for my duty

lines.speaker: KNIGHT
lines.text: cannot be silent when I think your highness wronged.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Thou but rememberest me of mine own conception: I have perceived

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: a most faint neglect of late; which I have rather blamed as mine

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: own jealous curiosity than as a very pretence and purpose of

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: unkindness: I will look further into’t. But where’s my fool? I

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: have not seen him this two days.

lines.speaker: KNIGHT
lines.text: Since my young lady’s going into France, sir, the fool hath much

lines.speaker: KNIGHT
lines.text: pined away.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: No more of that; I have noted it well. Go you and tell my

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: daughter I would speak with her.
[_Exit Attendant._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Go you, call hither my fool.
[_Exit another Attendant._]
Re-enter Oswald.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: O, you, sir, you, come you hither, sir: who am I, sir?

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: My lady’s father.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: My lady’s father! my lord’s knave: you whoreson dog! you slave! you

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: cur!

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: I am none of these, my lord; I beseech your pardon.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Do you bandy looks with me, you rascal?
[_Striking him._]

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: I’ll not be struck, my lord.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Nor tripp’d neither, you base football player.
[_Tripping up his heels._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I thank thee, fellow. Thou serv’st me, and I’ll love thee.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Come, sir, arise, away! I’ll teach you differences: away, away! If you

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: will measure your lubber’s length again, tarry; but away! go to; have

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: you wisdom? So.
[_Pushes Oswald out._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Now, my friendly knave, I thank thee: there’s earnest of thy service.
[_Giving Kent money._]
Enter Fool.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Let me hire him too; here’s my coxcomb.
[_Giving Kent his cap._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: How now, my pretty knave, how dost thou?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Sirrah, you were best take my coxcomb.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Why, fool?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Why, for taking one’s part that’s out of favour. Nay, an thou

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: canst not smile as the wind sits, thou’lt catch cold shortly:

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: there, take my coxcomb: why, this fellow has banish’d two on’s

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: daughters, and did the third a blessing against his will; if

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: thou follow him, thou must needs wear my coxcomb. How now,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: nuncle! Would I had two coxcombs and two daughters!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Why, my boy?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: If I gave them all my living, I’d keep my coxcombs myself. There’s

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: mine; beg another of thy daughters.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Take heed, sirrah, the whip.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Truth’s a dog must to kennel; he must be whipped out, when

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: the Lady Brach may stand by the fire and stink.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: A pestilent gall to me!

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Sirrah, I’ll teach thee a speech.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Do.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Mark it, nuncle:

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Have more than thou showest,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Speak less than thou knowest,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Lend less than thou owest,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Ride more than thou goest,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Learn more than thou trowest,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Set less than thou throwest;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Leave thy drink and thy whore,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: And keep in-a-door,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: And thou shalt have more

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Than two tens to a score.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: This is nothing, fool.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Then ’tis like the breath of an unfee’d lawyer, you gave me

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: nothing for’t. Can you make no use of nothing, nuncle?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Why, no, boy; nothing can be made out of nothing.
[_to Kent._]

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Prythee tell him, so much the rent of his land

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: comes to: he will not believe a fool.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: A bitter fool.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Dost thou know the difference, my boy, between a bitter fool and

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: a sweet one?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: No, lad; teach me.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: That lord that counsell’d thee

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: To give away thy land,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Come place him here by me,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Do thou for him stand.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: The sweet and bitter fool

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Will presently appear;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: The one in motley here,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: The other found out there.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Dost thou call me fool, boy?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: All thy other titles thou hast given away; that thou wast born

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: with.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: This is not altogether fool, my lord.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: No, faith; lords and great men will not let me; if I had a

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: monopoly out, they would have part on’t and ladies too, they

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: will not let me have all the fool to myself; they’ll be

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: snatching. Nuncle, give me an egg, and I’ll give thee two

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: crowns.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What two crowns shall they be?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Why, after I have cut the egg i’ the middle and eat up the

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: meat, the two crowns of the egg. When thou clovest thy crown i’

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: the middle and gav’st away both parts, thou bor’st thine ass on

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: thy back o’er the dirt: thou hadst little wit in thy bald crown

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: when thou gav’st thy golden one away. If I speak like myself in

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: this, let him be whipped that first finds it so.
[_Singing._]

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Fools had ne’er less grace in a year;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: For wise men are grown foppish,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: And know not how their wits to wear,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Their manners are so apish.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: When were you wont to be so full of songs, sirrah?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: I have used it, nuncle, e’er since thou mad’st thy daughters thy

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: mothers; for when thou gav’st them the rod, and put’st down thine

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: own breeches,
[_Singing._]

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Then they for sudden joy did weep,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: And I for sorrow sung,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: That such a king should play bo-peep,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: And go the fools among.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Prythee, nuncle, keep a schoolmaster that can teach thy fool to

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: lie; I would fain learn to lie.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: An you lie, sirrah, we’ll have you whipped.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: I marvel what kin thou and thy daughters are: they’ll have me

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: whipped for speaking true; thou’lt have me whipped for lying;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: and sometimes I am whipped for holding my peace. I had rather be

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: any kind o’thing than a fool: and yet I would not be thee,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: nuncle: thou hast pared thy wit o’both sides, and left nothing

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: i’ the middle: here comes one o’ the parings.
Enter Goneril.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: How now, daughter? What makes that frontlet on? Methinks you

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: are too much of late i’ the frown.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Thou wast a pretty fellow when thou hadst no need to care for

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: her frowning. Now thou art an O without a figure: I am better

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: than thou art now. I am a fool, thou art nothing.
[_To Goneril._]

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Yes, forsooth, I will hold my tongue. So your face bids me, though

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: you say nothing. Mum, mum,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: He that keeps nor crust nor crum,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Weary of all, shall want some.
[_Pointing to Lear_.]

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: That’s a shealed peascod.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Not only, sir, this your all-licens’d fool,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: But other of your insolent retinue

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Do hourly carp and quarrel; breaking forth

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: In rank and not-to-be-endured riots. Sir,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: I had thought, by making this well known unto you,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: To have found a safe redress; but now grow fearful,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: By what yourself too late have spoke and done,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: That you protect this course, and put it on

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: By your allowance; which if you should, the fault

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Would not scape censure, nor the redresses sleep,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Which, in the tender of a wholesome weal,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Might in their working do you that offence

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Which else were shame, that then necessity

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Will call discreet proceeding.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: For you know, nuncle,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: The hedge-sparrow fed the cuckoo so long

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: That it’s had it head bit off by it young.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: So out went the candle, and we were left darkling.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Are you our daughter?

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Come, sir,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: I would you would make use of that good wisdom,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Whereof I know you are fraught; and put away

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: These dispositions, which of late transform you

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: From what you rightly are.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: May not an ass know when the cart draws the horse? Whoop, Jug! I

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: love thee!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Doth any here know me? This is not Lear;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Doth Lear walk thus? speak thus? Where are his eyes?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Either his notion weakens, his discernings

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Are lethargied. Ha! waking? ’Tis not so!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Who is it that can tell me who I am?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Lear’s shadow.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I would learn that; for by the marks of sovereignty, knowledge and

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: reason, I should be false persuaded I had daughters.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Which they will make an obedient father.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Your name, fair gentlewoman?

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: This admiration, sir, is much o’ the favour

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Of other your new pranks. I do beseech you

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: To understand my purposes aright:

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: As you are old and reverend, you should be wise.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Here do you keep a hundred knights and squires;

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Men so disorder’d, so debosh’d and bold

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: That this our court, infected with their manners,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Shows like a riotous inn. Epicurism and lust

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Makes it more like a tavern or a brothel

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Than a grac’d palace. The shame itself doth speak

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: For instant remedy. Be, then, desir’d

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: By her that else will take the thing she begs

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: A little to disquantity your train;

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: And the remainder that shall still depend,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: To be such men as may besort your age,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Which know themselves, and you.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Darkness and devils!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Saddle my horses; call my train together.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Degenerate bastard! I’ll not trouble thee:

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Yet have I left a daughter.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: You strike my people; and your disorder’d rabble

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Make servants of their betters.
Enter Albany.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Woe that too late repents!—
[_To Albany._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: O, sir, are you come?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Is it your will? Speak, sir.—Prepare my horses.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Ingratitude, thou marble-hearted fiend,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: More hideous when thou show’st thee in a child

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Than the sea-monster!

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Pray, sir, be patient.
[_to Goneril._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Detested kite, thou liest.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: My train are men of choice and rarest parts,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That all particulars of duty know;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: And in the most exact regard support

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: The worships of their name. O most small fault,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: How ugly didst thou in Cordelia show!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Which, like an engine, wrench’d my frame of nature

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: From the fix’d place; drew from my heart all love,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: And added to the gall. O Lear, Lear, Lear!
[_Striking his head._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Beat at this gate that let thy folly in

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: And thy dear judgement out! Go, go, my people.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: My lord, I am guiltless, as I am ignorant

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Of what hath moved you.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: It may be so, my lord.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Hear, nature, hear; dear goddess, hear!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Suspend thy purpose, if thou didst intend

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: To make this creature fruitful!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Into her womb convey sterility!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Dry up in her the organs of increase;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: And from her derogate body never spring

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: A babe to honour her! If she must teem,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Create her child of spleen, that it may live

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: And be a thwart disnatur’d torment to her!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Let it stamp wrinkles in her brow of youth;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: With cadent tears fret channels in her cheeks;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Turn all her mother’s pains and benefits

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: To laughter and contempt; that she may feel

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: How sharper than a serpent’s tooth it is

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: To have a thankless child! Away, away!
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Now, gods that we adore, whereof comes this?

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Never afflict yourself to know more of it;

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: But let his disposition have that scope

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: That dotage gives it.
Re-enter Lear.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What, fifty of my followers at a clap?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Within a fortnight?

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: What’s the matter, sir?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I’ll tell thee. [_To Goneril._] Life and death! I am

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: asham’d

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That thou hast power to shake my manhood thus;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That these hot tears, which break from me perforce,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Should make thee worth them. Blasts and fogs upon thee!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Th’untented woundings of a father’s curse

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Pierce every sense about thee! Old fond eyes,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Beweep this cause again, I’ll pluck ye out,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: And cast you with the waters that you lose

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: To temper clay. Ha! Let it be so.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I have another daughter,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Who, I am sure, is kind and comfortable:

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: When she shall hear this of thee, with her nails

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: She’ll flay thy wolvish visage. Thou shalt find

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That I’ll resume the shape which thou dost think

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I have cast off for ever.
[_Exeunt Lear, Kent and Attendants._]

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Do you mark that?

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: I cannot be so partial, Goneril,

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: To the great love I bear you,—

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Pray you, content. What, Oswald, ho!
[_To the Fool._]

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: You, sir, more knave than fool, after your master.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Nuncle Lear, nuncle Lear, tarry and take the fool with thee.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: A fox when one has caught her,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: And such a daughter,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Should sure to the slaughter,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: If my cap would buy a halter;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: So the fool follows after.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: This man hath had good counsel.—A hundred knights!

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: ’Tis politic and safe to let him keep

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: At point a hundred knights: yes, that on every dream,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Each buzz, each fancy, each complaint, dislike,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: He may enguard his dotage with their powers,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: And hold our lives in mercy. Oswald, I say!

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Well, you may fear too far.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Safer than trust too far:

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Let me still take away the harms I fear,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Not fear still to be taken: I know his heart.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: What he hath utter’d I have writ my sister:

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: If she sustain him and his hundred knights,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: When I have show’d th’unfitness,—
Re-enter Oswald.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: How now, Oswald!

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: What, have you writ that letter to my sister?

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: Ay, madam.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Take you some company, and away to horse:

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Inform her full of my particular fear;

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: And thereto add such reasons of your own

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: As may compact it more. Get you gone;

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: And hasten your return.
[_Exit Oswald._]

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: No, no, my lord!

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: This milky gentleness and course of yours,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Though I condemn not, yet, under pardon,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: You are much more attask’d for want of wisdom

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Than prais’d for harmful mildness.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: How far your eyes may pierce I cannot tell:

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Striving to better, oft we mar what’s well.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Nay then,—

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Well, well; the event.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Court before the Duke of Albany’s Palace

lines.text: Enter Lear, Kent and Fool.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Go you before to Gloucester with these letters: acquaint my

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: daughter no further with anything you know than comes from her

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: demand out of the letter. If your diligence be not speedy, I

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: shall be there afore you.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: I will not sleep, my lord, till I have delivered your letter.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: If a man’s brains were in’s heels, were’t not in danger of

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: kibes?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Ay, boy.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Then I prythee be merry; thy wit shall not go slipshod.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Ha, ha, ha!

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Shalt see thy other daughter will use thee kindly, for though

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: she’s as like this as a crab’s like an apple, yet I can tell

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: what I can tell.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What canst tell, boy?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: She’ll taste as like this as a crab does to a crab. Thou

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: canst tell why one’s nose stands i’the middle on’s face?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Why, to keep one’s eyes of either side’s nose, that what a man

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: cannot smell out, he may spy into.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I did her wrong.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Canst tell how an oyster makes his shell?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Nor I neither; but I can tell why a snail has a house.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Why, to put’s head in; not to give it away to his daughters, and

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: leave his horns without a case.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I will forget my nature. So kind a father! Be my horses ready?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Thy asses are gone about ’em. The reason why the seven stars are

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: no more than seven is a pretty reason.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Because they are not eight?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Yes indeed: thou wouldst make a good fool.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: To tak’t again perforce!—Monster ingratitude!

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: If thou wert my fool, nuncle, I’d have thee beaten for being

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: old before thy time.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: How’s that?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Thou shouldst not have been old till thou hadst been wise.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: O, let me not be mad, not mad, sweet heaven!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Keep me in temper; I would not be mad!
Enter Gentleman.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: How now? are the horses ready?

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Ready, my lord.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Come, boy.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: She that’s a maid now, and laughs at my departure,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Shall not be a maid long, unless things be cut shorter.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A court within the Castle of the Earl of Gloucester

lines.text: Enter Edmund and Curan, meeting.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Save thee, Curan.

lines.speaker: CURAN
lines.text: And you, sir. I have been with your father, and given him

lines.speaker: CURAN
lines.text: notice that the Duke of Cornwall and Regan his Duchess will be

lines.speaker: CURAN
lines.text: here with him this night.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: How comes that?

lines.speaker: CURAN
lines.text: Nay, I know not. You have heard of the news abroad; I mean the

lines.speaker: CURAN
lines.text: whispered ones, for they are yet but ear-kissing arguments?

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Not I: pray you, what are they?

lines.speaker: CURAN

Enter Kent and Oswald, severally.

lines.text: Good dawning to thee, friend: art of this house?

lines.text: I’ the mire.

lines.text: worsted-stocking knave; a lily-livered, action-taking, whoreson,

lines.text: shines; I’ll make a sop o’ the moonshine of you: draw, you

lines.speaker: KENT

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: Away! I have nothing to do with thee.

lines.text: Help, ho! murder! help!

lines.text: Help, ho! murder! murder!

lines.text: No more perchance does mine, or his, or hers.

lines.text: Sir, ’tis my occupation to be plain:
