lines.text: If only to go warm were gorgeous,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Why, nature needs not what thou gorgeous wear’st

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Which scarcely keeps thee warm. But, for true need,—

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: You heavens, give me that patience, patience I need!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: You see me here, you gods, a poor old man,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: As full of grief as age; wretched in both!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: If it be you that stirs these daughters’ hearts

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Against their father, fool me not so much

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: To bear it tamely; touch me with noble anger,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: And let not women’s weapons, water-drops,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Stain my man’s cheeks! No, you unnatural hags,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I will have such revenges on you both

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That all the world shall,—I will do such things,—

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What they are yet, I know not; but they shall be

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: The terrors of the earth. You think I’ll weep;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: No, I’ll not weep:—
[_Storm and tempest._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I have full cause of weeping; but this heart

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Shall break into a hundred thousand flaws

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Or ere I’ll weep.—O fool, I shall go mad!
[_Exeunt Lear, Gloucester, Kent and Fool._]

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Let us withdraw; ’twill be a storm.

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: This house is little: the old man and his people

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Cannot be well bestow’d.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: ’Tis his own blame; hath put himself from rest

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: And must needs taste his folly.

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: For his particular, I’ll receive him gladly,

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: But not one follower.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: So am I purpos’d.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Where is my lord of Gloucester?
Enter Gloucester.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Followed the old man forth, he is return’d.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: The King is in high rage.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Whither is he going?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: He calls to horse; but will I know not whither.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: ’Tis best to give him way; he leads himself.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: My lord, entreat him by no means to stay.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Alack, the night comes on, and the high winds

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Do sorely ruffle; for many miles about

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: There’s scarce a bush.

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: O, sir, to wilful men

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: The injuries that they themselves procure

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Must be their schoolmasters. Shut up your doors.

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: He is attended with a desperate train,

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: And what they may incense him to, being apt

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: To have his ear abus’d, wisdom bids fear.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Shut up your doors, my lord; ’tis a wild night.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: My Regan counsels well: come out o’ the storm.
[_Exeunt._]
A storm with thunder and lightning. Enter Kent and a Gentleman, severally.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Who’s there, besides foul weather?

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: One minded like the weather, most unquietly.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: I know you. Where’s the King?

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Contending with the fretful elements;

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Bids the wind blow the earth into the sea,

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Or swell the curled waters ’bove the main,

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: That things might change or cease; tears his white hair,

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Which the impetuous blasts with eyeless rage,

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Catch in their fury and make nothing of;

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Strives in his little world of man to outscorn

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: The to-and-fro-conflicting wind and rain.

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: This night, wherein the cub-drawn bear would couch,

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: The lion and the belly-pinched wolf

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Keep their fur dry, unbonneted he runs,

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: And bids what will take all.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: But who is with him?

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: None but the fool, who labours to out-jest

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: His heart-struck injuries.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Sir, I do know you;

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: And dare, upon the warrant of my note

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Commend a dear thing to you. There is division,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Although as yet the face of it be cover’d

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: With mutual cunning, ’twixt Albany and Cornwall;

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Who have, as who have not, that their great stars

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Throne’d and set high; servants, who seem no less,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Which are to France the spies and speculations

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Intelligent of our state. What hath been seen,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Either in snuffs and packings of the Dukes;

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Or the hard rein which both of them have borne

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Against the old kind King; or something deeper,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Whereof, perchance, these are but furnishings;—

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: But, true it is, from France there comes a power

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Into this scatter’d kingdom; who already,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Wise in our negligence, have secret feet

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: In some of our best ports, and are at point

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: To show their open banner.—Now to you:

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: If on my credit you dare build so far

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: To make your speed to Dover, you shall find

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Some that will thank you making just report

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Of how unnatural and bemadding sorrow

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: The King hath cause to plain.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: I am a gentleman of blood and breeding;

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: And from some knowledge and assurance

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Offer this office to you.

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: I will talk further with you.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: No, do not.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: For confirmation that I am much more

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Than my out-wall, open this purse, and take

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: What it contains. If you shall see Cordelia,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: As fear not but you shall, show her this ring;

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: And she will tell you who your fellow is

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: That yet you do not know. Fie on this storm!

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: I will go seek the King.

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Give me your hand: have you no more to say?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Few words, but, to effect, more than all yet:

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: That, when we have found the King, in which your pain

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: That way, I’ll this; he that first lights on him

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Holla the other.
[_Exeunt._]
Storm continues. Enter Lear and Fool.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Blow, winds, and crack your cheeks! Rage! blow!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: You cataracts and hurricanoes, spout

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Till you have drench’d our steeples, drown’d the cocks!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: You sulphurous and thought-executing fires,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Vaunt-couriers to oak-cleaving thunderbolts,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Singe my white head! And thou, all-shaking thunder,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Strike flat the thick rotundity o’ the world!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Crack nature’s moulds, all germens spill at once,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That make ingrateful man!

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: O nuncle, court holy-water in a dry house is better than this

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: rain-water out o’ door. Good nuncle, in; and ask thy daughters

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: blessing: here’s a night pities neither wise men nor fools.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Rumble thy bellyful! Spit, fire! spout, rain!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Nor rain, wind, thunder, fire are my daughters;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I tax not you, you elements, with unkindness.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I never gave you kingdom, call’d you children;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: You owe me no subscription: then let fall

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Your horrible pleasure. Here I stand your slave,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: A poor, infirm, weak, and despis’d old man:

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: But yet I call you servile ministers,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That will with two pernicious daughters join

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Your high-engender’d battles ’gainst a head

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: So old and white as this! O! O! ’tis foul!

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: He that has a house to put’s head in has a good head-piece.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: The codpiece that will house

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Before the head has any,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: The head and he shall louse:

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: So beggars marry many.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: The man that makes his toe

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: What he his heart should make

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Shall of a corn cry woe,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: And turn his sleep to wake.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: For there was never yet fair woman but she made mouths in a glass.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: No, I will be the pattern of all patience;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I will say nothing.
Enter Kent.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Who’s there?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Marry, here’s grace and a codpiece; that’s a wise man and a

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: fool.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Alas, sir, are you here? Things that love night

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Love not such nights as these; the wrathful skies

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Gallow the very wanderers of the dark,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: And make them keep their caves. Since I was man,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Such sheets of fire, such bursts of horrid thunder,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Such groans of roaring wind and rain I never

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Remember to have heard. Man’s nature cannot carry

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Th’affliction, nor the fear.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Let the great gods,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That keep this dreadful pudder o’er our heads,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Find out their enemies now. Tremble, thou wretch,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That hast within thee undivulged crimes

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Unwhipp’d of justice. Hide thee, thou bloody hand;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Thou perjur’d, and thou simular of virtue

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That art incestuous. Caitiff, to pieces shake

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That under covert and convenient seeming

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Hast practis’d on man’s life: close pent-up guilts,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Rive your concealing continents, and cry

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: These dreadful summoners grace. I am a man

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: More sinn’d against than sinning.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Alack, bareheaded!

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Gracious my lord, hard by here is a hovel;

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Some friendship will it lend you ’gainst the tempest:

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Repose you there, whilst I to this hard house,—

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: More harder than the stones whereof ’tis rais’d;

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Which even but now, demanding after you,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Denied me to come in,—return, and force

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Their scanted courtesy.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: My wits begin to turn.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Come on, my boy. How dost, my boy? Art cold?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I am cold myself. Where is this straw, my fellow?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: The art of our necessities is strange,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That can make vile things precious. Come, your hovel.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Poor fool and knave, I have one part in my heart

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That’s sorry yet for thee.
[_Singing._]

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: He that has and a little tiny wit,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: With heigh-ho, the wind and the rain,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Must make content with his fortunes fit,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Though the rain it raineth every day.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: True, boy. Come, bring us to this hovel.
[_Exeunt Lear and Kent._]

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: This is a brave night to cool a courtezan. I’ll speak a prophecy

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: ere I go:

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: When priests are more in word than matter;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: When brewers mar their malt with water;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: When nobles are their tailors’ tutors;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: No heretics burn’d, but wenches’ suitors;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: When every case in law is right;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: No squire in debt, nor no poor knight;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: When slanders do not live in tongues;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Nor cut-purses come not to throngs;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: When usurers tell their gold i’ the field;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: And bawds and whores do churches build,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Then shall the realm of Albion

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Come to great confusion:

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Then comes the time, who lives to see’t,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: That going shall be us’d with feet.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: This prophecy Merlin shall make; for I live before his time.
[_Exit._]
Enter Gloucester and Edmund.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Alack, alack, Edmund, I like not this unnatural dealing. When I

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: desired their leave that I might pity him, they took from me the

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: use of mine own house; charged me on pain of perpetual displeasure,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: neither to speak of him, entreat for him, or any way sustain him.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Most savage and unnatural!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Go to; say you nothing. There is division between the Dukes,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: and a worse matter than that: I have received a letter this

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: night;—’tis dangerous to be spoken;—I have locked the letter

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: in my closet: these injuries the King now bears will be revenged

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: home; there’s part of a power already footed: we must incline to

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: the King. I will look him, and privily relieve him: go you and

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: maintain talk with the Duke, that my charity be not of him

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: perceived: if he ask for me, I am ill, and gone to bed. If I

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: die for it, as no less is threatened me, the King my old master

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: must be relieved. There is some strange thing toward, Edmund;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: pray you be careful.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: This courtesy, forbid thee, shall the Duke

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Instantly know; and of that letter too.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: This seems a fair deserving, and must draw me

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: That which my father loses, no less than all:

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: The younger rises when the old doth fall.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: A part of the Heath with a Hovel

lines.text: Storm continues. Enter Lear, Kent and Fool.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Here is the place, my lord; good my lord, enter:

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: The tyranny of the open night’s too rough

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: For nature to endure.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Let me alone.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Good my lord, enter here.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Wilt break my heart?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: I had rather break mine own. Good my lord, enter.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Thou think’st ’tis much that this contentious storm

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Invades us to the skin: so ’tis to thee,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: But where the greater malady is fix’d,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: The lesser is scarce felt. Thou’dst shun a bear;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: But if thy flight lay toward the raging sea,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Thou’dst meet the bear i’ the mouth. When the mind’s

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: free,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: The body’s delicate: the tempest in my mind

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Doth from my senses take all feeling else

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Save what beats there. Filial ingratitude!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Is it not as this mouth should tear this hand

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: For lifting food to’t? But I will punish home;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: No, I will weep no more. In such a night

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: To shut me out! Pour on; I will endure:

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: In such a night as this! O Regan, Goneril!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Your old kind father, whose frank heart gave all,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: O, that way madness lies; let me shun that;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: No more of that.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Good my lord, enter here.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Prythee go in thyself; seek thine own ease:

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: This tempest will not give me leave to ponder

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: On things would hurt me more. But I’ll go in.
[_To the Fool._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: In, boy; go first. You houseless poverty,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Nay, get thee in. I’ll pray, and then I’ll sleep.
[_Fool goes in._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Poor naked wretches, wheresoe’er you are,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That bide the pelting of this pitiless storm,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: How shall your houseless heads and unfed sides,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Your loop’d and window’d raggedness, defend you

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: From seasons such as these? O, I have ta’en

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Too little care of this! Take physic, pomp;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Expose thyself to feel what wretches feel,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That thou mayst shake the superflux to them

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: And show the heavens more just.
[_Within._]

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Fathom and half, fathom and half! Poor Tom!
[_The Fool runs out from the hovel._]

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Come not in here, nuncle, here’s a spirit.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Help me, help me!

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Give me thy hand. Who’s there?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: A spirit, a spirit: he says his name’s poor Tom.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: What art thou that dost grumble there i’ the straw?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Come forth.
Enter Edgar, disguised as a madman.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Away! the foul fiend follows me! Through the sharp hawthorn blows the

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: cold wind. Humh! go to thy cold bed, and warm thee.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Didst thou give all to thy two daughters?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: And art thou come to this?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Who gives anything to poor Tom? Whom the foul fiend hath led

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: through fire and through flame, through ford and whirlpool, o’er

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: bog and quagmire; that hath laid knives under his pillow and

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: halters in his pew, set ratsbane by his porridge; made him proud

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: of heart, to ride on a bay trotting horse over four-inched

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: bridges, to course his own shadow for a traitor. Bless thy five

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: wits! 	Tom’s a-cold. O, do, de, do, de, do, de. Bless thee from

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: whirlwinds, star-blasting, and taking! Do poor Tom some charity,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: whom the foul fiend vexes. There could I have him now, and

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: there,—and there again, and there.
[_Storm continues._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What, have his daughters brought him to this pass?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Couldst thou save nothing? Didst thou give ’em all?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Nay, he reserv’d a blanket, else we had been all shamed.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Now all the plagues that in the pendulous air

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Hang fated o’er men’s faults light on thy daughters!

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: He hath no daughters, sir.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Death, traitor! nothing could have subdu’d nature

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: To such a lowness but his unkind daughters.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Is it the fashion that discarded fathers

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Should have thus little mercy on their flesh?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Judicious punishment! ’twas this flesh begot

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Those pelican daughters.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Pillicock sat on Pillicock hill,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Alow, alow, loo loo!

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: This cold night will turn us all to fools and madmen.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Take heed o’ th’ foul fiend: obey thy parents; keep thy word

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: justly; swear not; commit not with man’s sworn spouse; set not

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: thy sweet-heart on proud array. Tom’s a-cold.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What hast thou been?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: A serving-man, proud in heart and mind; that curled my hair;

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: wore gloves in my cap; served the lust of my mistress’ heart, and

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: did the act of darkness with her; swore as many oaths as I spake

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: words, and broke them in the sweet face of heaven. One that

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: slept in the contriving of lust, and waked to do it. Wine loved

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: I deeply, dice dearly; and in woman out-paramour’d the Turk.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: False of heart, light of ear, bloody of hand; hog in sloth, fox

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: in stealth, wolf in greediness, dog in madness, lion in prey.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Let not the creaking of shoes nor the rustling of silks betray

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: thy poor heart to woman. Keep thy foot out of brothels, thy hand

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: out of plackets, thy pen from lender’s book, and defy the foul

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: fiend. Still through the hawthorn blows the cold wind: says

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: suum, mun, nonny. Dolphin my boy, boy, sessa! let him trot by.
[_Storm still continues._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Why, thou wert better in thy grave than to answer with thy uncovered

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: body this extremity of the skies. Is man no more than this? Consider

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: him well. Thou owest the worm no silk, the beast no hide, the sheep no

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: wool, the cat no perfume. Ha! here’s three on’s are

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: sophisticated! Thou art the thing itself: unaccommodated man is no more

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: but such a poor, bare, forked animal as thou art. Off, off, you

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: lendings! Come, unbutton here.
[_Tears off his clothes._]

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Prythee, nuncle, be contented; ’tis a naughty night to swim

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: in. Now a little fire in a wild field were like an old lecher’s

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: heart, a small spark, all the rest on’s body cold. Look, here

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: comes a walking fire.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: This is the foul fiend Flibbertigibbet: he begins at curfew, and walks

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: till the first cock; he gives the web and the pin, squints the eye, and

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: makes the harelip; mildews the white wheat, and hurts the poor creature

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: of earth.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Swithold footed thrice the old;

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: He met the nightmare, and her nine-fold;

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Bid her alight and her troth plight,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: And aroint thee, witch, aroint thee!

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: How fares your grace?
Enter Gloucester with a torch.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What’s he?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Who’s there? What is’t you seek?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: What are you there? Your names?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Poor Tom; that eats the swimming frog, the toad, the todpole, the

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: wall-newt and the water; that in the fury of his heart, when the

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: foul fiend rages, eats cow-dung for sallets; swallows the old rat

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: and the ditch-dog; drinks the green mantle of the standing pool;

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: who is whipped from tithing to tithing, and stocked, punished,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: and imprisoned; who hath had three suits to his back, six shirts

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: to his body,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Horse to ride, and weapon to wear.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: But mice and rats and such small deer,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Have been Tom’s food for seven long year.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Beware my follower. Peace, Smulkin; peace, thou fiend!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: What, hath your grace no better company?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: The prince of darkness is a gentleman:

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Modo he’s call’d, and Mahu.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Our flesh and blood, my lord, is grown so vile

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: That it doth hate what gets it.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Poor Tom’s a-cold.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Go in with me: my duty cannot suffer

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: T’obey in all your daughters’ hard commands;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Though their injunction be to bar my doors,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And let this tyrannous night take hold upon you,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Yet have I ventur’d to come seek you out,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And bring you where both fire and food is ready.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: First let me talk with this philosopher.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What is the cause of thunder?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Good my lord, take his offer; go into the house.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I’ll talk a word with this same learned Theban.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What is your study?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: How to prevent the fiend and to kill vermin.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Let me ask you one word in private.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Importune him once more to go, my lord;

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: His wits begin t’unsettle.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Canst thou blame him?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: His daughters seek his death. Ah, that good Kent!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: He said it would be thus, poor banish’d man!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thou sayest the King grows mad; I’ll tell thee, friend,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I am almost mad myself. I had a son,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Now outlaw’d from my blood; he sought my life

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: But lately, very late: I lov’d him, friend,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: No father his son dearer: true to tell thee,
[_Storm continues._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: The grief hath craz’d my wits. What a night’s this!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I do beseech your grace.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: O, cry you mercy, sir.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Noble philosopher, your company.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Tom’s a-cold.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: In, fellow, there, into the hovel; keep thee warm.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Come, let’s in all.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: This way, my lord.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: With him;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I will keep still with my philosopher.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Good my lord, soothe him; let him take the fellow.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Take him you on.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Sirrah, come on; go along with us.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Come, good Athenian.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: No words, no words, hush.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Child Rowland to the dark tower came,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: His word was still—Fie, foh, and fum,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: I smell the blood of a British man.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Cornwall and Edmund.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: I will have my revenge ere I depart his house.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: How, my lord, I may be censured, that nature thus gives way to

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: loyalty, something fears me to think of.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: I now perceive it was not altogether your brother’s evil

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: disposition made him seek his death; but a provoking merit, set

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: a-work by a reproveable badness in himself.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: How malicious is my fortune, that I must repent to be just! This

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: is the letter he spoke of, which approves him an intelligent

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: party to the advantages of France. O heavens! that this treason

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: were not; or not I the detector!

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Go with me to the Duchess.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: If the matter of this paper be certain, you have mighty business

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: in hand.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: True or false, it hath made thee Earl of Gloucester. Seek out

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: where thy father is, that he may be ready for our apprehension.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: If I find him comforting the King, it will stuff his

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: suspicion more fully. I will persever in my course of loyalty,

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: though the conflict be sore between that and my blood.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: I will lay trust upon thee; and thou shalt find a dearer father

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: in my love.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A Chamber in a Farmhouse adjoining the Castle

lines.text: Enter Gloucester, Lear, Kent, Fool and Edgar.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Here is better than the open air; take it thankfully. I will

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: piece out the comfort with what addition I can: I will not be

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: long from you.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: All the power of his wits have given way to his impatience:—

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: the gods reward your kindness!
[_Exit Gloucester._]

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Frateretto calls me; and tells me Nero is an angler in the lake

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: of darkness. Pray, innocent, and beware the foul fiend.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Prythee, nuncle, tell me whether a madman be a gentleman or a

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: yeoman.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: A king, a king!

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: No, he’s a yeoman that has a gentleman to his son; for he’s a mad

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: yeoman that sees his son a gentleman before him.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: To have a thousand with red burning spits

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Come hissing in upon ’em.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: The foul fiend bites my back.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: He’s mad that trusts in the tameness of a wolf, a horse’s health,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: a boy’s love, or a whore’s oath.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: It shall be done; I will arraign them straight.
[_To Edgar._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Come, sit thou here, most learned justicer;
[_To the Fool._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Thou, sapient sir, sit here. Now, you she-foxes!—

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Look, where he stands and glares! Want’st thou eyes at trial, madam?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Come o’er the bourn, Bessy, to me.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Her boat hath a leak,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: And she must not speak

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Why she dares not come over to thee.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: The foul fiend haunts poor Tom in the voice of a nightingale.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Hoppedance cries in Tom’s belly for two white herring. Croak not, black

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: angel; I have no food for thee.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: How do you, sir? Stand you not so amaz’d;

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Will you lie down and rest upon the cushions?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I’ll see their trial first. Bring in their evidence.
[_To Edgar._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Thou, robed man of justice, take thy place.
[_To the Fool._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: And thou, his yokefellow of equity,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Bench by his side. [_To Kent._] You are o’ the commission,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Sit you too.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Let us deal justly.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Sleepest or wakest thou, jolly shepherd?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Thy sheep be in the corn;

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: And for one blast of thy minikin mouth

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Thy sheep shall take no harm.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Purr! the cat is grey.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Arraign her first; ’tis Goneril. I here take my oath before

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: this honourable assembly, she kicked the poor King her father.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Come hither, mistress. Is your name Goneril?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: She cannot deny it.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Cry you mercy, I took you for a joint-stool.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: And here’s another, whose warp’d looks proclaim

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What store her heart is made on. Stop her there!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Arms, arms! sword! fire! Corruption in the place!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: False justicer, why hast thou let her ’scape?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Bless thy five wits!

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: O pity! Sir, where is the patience now

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: That you so oft have boasted to retain?
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: My tears begin to take his part so much

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: They mar my counterfeiting.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: The little dogs and all,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Trey, Blanch, and Sweetheart, see, they bark at me.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Tom will throw his head at them. Avaunt, you curs!

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Be thy mouth or black or white,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Tooth that poisons if it bite;

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Mastiff, greyhound, mongrel grim,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Hound or spaniel, brach or him,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Or bobtail tike or trundle-tail,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Tom will make them weep and wail;

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: For, with throwing thus my head,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Dogs leap the hatch, and all are fled.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Do, de, de, de. Sessa! Come, march to wakes and fairs and market towns.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Poor Tom, thy horn is dry.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Then let them anatomize Regan; see what breeds about her

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: heart. Is there any cause in nature that makes these hard

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: hearts? [_To Edgar._] You, sir, I entertain you for one of my

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: hundred; only I do not like the fashion of your garments. You’ll

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: say they are Persian; but let them be changed.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Now, good my lord, lie here and rest awhile.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Make no noise, make no noise; draw the curtains.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: So, so. We’ll go to supper i’ the morning.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: And I’ll go to bed at noon.
Enter Gloucester.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Come hither, friend;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Where is the King my master?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Here, sir; but trouble him not, his wits are gone.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Good friend, I prythee, take him in thy arms;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I have o’erheard a plot of death upon him;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: There is a litter ready; lay him in’t

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And drive towards Dover, friend, where thou shalt meet

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Both welcome and protection. Take up thy master;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: If thou shouldst dally half an hour, his life,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: With thine, and all that offer to defend him,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Stand in assured loss. Take up, take up;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And follow me, that will to some provision

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Give thee quick conduct.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Oppressed nature sleeps.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: This rest might yet have balm’d thy broken sinews,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Which, if convenience will not allow,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Stand in hard cure. Come, help to bear thy master;
[_To the Fool._]

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Thou must not stay behind.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Come, come, away!
[_Exeunt Kent, Gloucester and the Fool bearing off Lear._]

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: When we our betters see bearing our woes,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: We scarcely think our miseries our foes.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Who alone suffers, suffers most i’ the mind,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Leaving free things and happy shows behind:

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: But then the mind much sufferance doth o’erskip

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: When grief hath mates, and bearing fellowship.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: How light and portable my pain seems now,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: When that which makes me bend makes the King bow;

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: He childed as I fathered! Tom, away!

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Mark the high noises; and thyself bewray,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: When false opinion, whose wrong thoughts defile thee,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: In thy just proof repeals and reconciles thee.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: What will hap more tonight, safe ’scape the King!

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Lurk, lurk.
[_Exit._]
Enter Cornwall, Regan, Goneril, Edmund and Servants.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Post speedily to my lord your husband, show him this letter: the army

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: of France is landed. Seek out the traitor Gloucester.
[_Exeunt some of the Servants._]

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Hang him instantly.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Pluck out his eyes.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Leave him to my displeasure. Edmund, keep you our sister

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: company: the revenges we are bound to take upon your traitorous

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: father are not fit for your beholding. Advise the Duke where you

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: are going, to a most festinate preparation: we are bound to the

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: like. Our posts shall be swift and intelligent betwixt us.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Farewell, dear sister, farewell, my lord of Gloucester.
Enter Oswald.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: How now! Where’s the King?

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: My lord of Gloucester hath convey’d him hence:

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: Some five or six and thirty of his knights,

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: Hot questrists after him, met him at gate;

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: Who, with some other of the lord’s dependants,

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: Are gone with him toward Dover: where they boast

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: To have well-armed friends.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Get horses for your mistress.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Farewell, sweet lord, and sister.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Edmund, farewell.
[_Exeunt Goneril, Edmund and Oswald._]

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Go seek the traitor Gloucester,

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Pinion him like a thief, bring him before us.
[_Exeunt other Servants._]

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Though well we may not pass upon his life

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Without the form of justice, yet our power

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Shall do a courtesy to our wrath, which men

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: May blame, but not control. Who’s there? The traitor?
Enter Gloucester and Servants.

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Ingrateful fox! ’tis he.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Bind fast his corky arms.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: What mean your graces?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Good my friends, consider you are my guests.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Do me no foul play, friends.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Bind him, I say.
[_Servants bind him._]

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Hard, hard. O filthy traitor!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Unmerciful lady as you are, I’m none.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: To this chair bind him. Villain, thou shalt find—
[_Regan plucks his beard._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: By the kind gods, ’tis most ignobly done

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To pluck me by the beard.

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: So white, and such a traitor!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Naughty lady,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: These hairs which thou dost ravish from my chin

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Will quicken, and accuse thee. I am your host:

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: With robber’s hands my hospitable favours

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: You should not ruffle thus. What will you do?

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Come, sir, what letters had you late from France?

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Be simple answer’d, for we know the truth.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: And what confederacy have you with the traitors,

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Late footed in the kingdom?

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: To whose hands have you sent the lunatic King?

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Speak.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I have a letter guessingly set down,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Which came from one that’s of a neutral heart,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And not from one oppos’d.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Cunning.

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: And false.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Where hast thou sent the King?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To Dover.

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Wherefore to Dover? Wast thou not charg’d at peril,—

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Wherefore to Dover? Let him first answer that.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I am tied to the stake, and I must stand the course.

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Wherefore to Dover, sir?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Because I would not see thy cruel nails

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Pluck out his poor old eyes; nor thy fierce sister

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: In his anointed flesh stick boarish fangs.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: The sea, with such a storm as his bare head

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: In hell-black night endur’d, would have buoy’d up,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And quench’d the stelled fires;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Yet, poor old heart, he holp the heavens to rain.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: If wolves had at thy gate howl’d that stern time,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thou shouldst have said, ‘Good porter, turn the key.’

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: All cruels else subscrib’d: but I shall see

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: The winged vengeance overtake such children.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: See’t shalt thou never. Fellows, hold the chair.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Upon these eyes of thine I’ll set my foot.
[_Gloucester is held down in his chair, while Cornwall plucks out one of his eyes and sets his foot on it._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: He that will think to live till he be old,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Give me some help!—O cruel! O you gods!

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: One side will mock another; the other too!

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: If you see vengeance—

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
lines.text: Hold your hand, my lord:

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
lines.text: I have serv’d you ever since I was a child;

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
lines.text: But better service have I never done you

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
lines.text: Than now to bid you hold.

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: How now, you dog!

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
lines.text: If you did wear a beard upon your chin,

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
lines.text: I’d shake it on this quarrel. What do you mean?

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: My villain?
[_Draws, and runs at him._]

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
lines.text: Nay, then, come on, and take the chance of anger.
[_Draws. They fight. Cornwall is wounded._]
[_To another servant._]

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Give me thy sword. A peasant stand up thus?
[_Snatches a sword, comes behind, and stabs him._]

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
lines.text: O, I am slain! My lord, you have one eye left

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
lines.text: To see some mischief on him. O!
[_Dies._]

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Lest it see more, prevent it. Out, vile jelly!

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Where is thy lustre now?
[_Tears out Gloucester’s other eye and throws it on the ground._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: All dark and comfortless. Where’s my son Edmund?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Edmund, enkindle all the sparks of nature

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To quit this horrid act.

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Out, treacherous villain!

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Thou call’st on him that hates thee: it was he

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: That made the overture of thy treasons to us;

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Who is too good to pity thee.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: O my follies! Then Edgar was abus’d.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Kind gods, forgive me that, and prosper him!

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: Go thrust him out at gates, and let him smell

lines.speaker: REGAN
lines.text: His way to Dover. How is’t, my lord? How look you?

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: I have receiv’d a hurt: follow me, lady.

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Turn out that eyeless villain. Throw this slave

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Upon the dunghill. Regan, I bleed apace:

lines.speaker: CORNWALL
lines.text: Untimely comes this hurt: give me your arm.
[_Exit Cornwall, led by Regan; Servants unbind Gloucester and lead him out._]

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
lines.text: I’ll never care what wickedness I do,

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
lines.text: If this man come to good.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVANT
lines.text: If she live long,

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVANT
lines.text: And in the end meet the old course of death,

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVANT
lines.text: Women will all turn monsters.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
lines.text: Let’s follow the old Earl, and get the bedlam

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
lines.text: To lead him where he would: his roguish madness

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
lines.text: Allows itself to anything.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVANT
lines.text: Go thou: I’ll fetch some flax and whites of eggs

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVANT
lines.text: To apply to his bleeding face. Now heaven help him!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Edgar.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Yet better thus, and known to be contemn’d,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Than still contemn’d and flatter’d. To be worst,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: The lowest and most dejected thing of fortune,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Stands still in esperance, lives not in fear:

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: The lamentable change is from the best;

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: The worst returns to laughter. Welcome then,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Thou unsubstantial air that I embrace;

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: The wretch that thou hast blown unto the worst

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Owes nothing to thy blasts.
Enter Gloucester, led by an Old Man.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: But who comes here? My father, poorly led?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: World, world, O world!

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: But that thy strange mutations make us hate thee,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Life would not yield to age.

lines.speaker: OLD MAN
lines.text: O my good lord, I have been your tenant, and your father’s tenant

lines.speaker: OLD MAN
lines.text: these fourscore years.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Away, get thee away; good friend, be gone.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thy comforts can do me no good at all;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thee they may hurt.

lines.speaker: OLD MAN
lines.text: You cannot see your way.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I have no way, and therefore want no eyes;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I stumbled when I saw. Full oft ’tis seen

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Our means secure us, and our mere defects

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Prove our commodities. O dear son Edgar,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: The food of thy abused father’s wrath!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Might I but live to see thee in my touch,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I’d say I had eyes again!

lines.speaker: OLD MAN
lines.text: How now! Who’s there?
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: O gods! Who is’t can say ‘I am at the

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: worst’?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: I am worse than e’er I was.

lines.speaker: OLD MAN
lines.text: ’Tis poor mad Tom.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: And worse I may be yet. The worst is not

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: So long as we can say ‘This is the worst.’

lines.speaker: OLD MAN
lines.text: Fellow, where goest?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Is it a beggar-man?

lines.speaker: OLD MAN
lines.text: Madman, and beggar too.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: He has some reason, else he could not beg.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I’ the last night’s storm I such a fellow saw;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Which made me think a man a worm. My son

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Came then into my mind, and yet my mind

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Was then scarce friends with him.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I have heard more since.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: As flies to wanton boys are we to the gods,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: They kill us for their sport.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: How should this be?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Bad is the trade that must play fool to sorrow,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Angering itself and others. Bless thee, master!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Is that the naked fellow?

lines.speaker: OLD MAN
lines.text: Ay, my lord.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Then prythee get thee away. If for my sake

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thou wilt o’ertake us hence a mile or twain,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I’ the way toward Dover, do it for ancient love,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And bring some covering for this naked soul,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Which I’ll entreat to lead me.

lines.speaker: OLD MAN
lines.text: Alack, sir, he is mad.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: ’Tis the time’s plague when madmen lead the blind.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Do as I bid thee, or rather do thy pleasure;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Above the rest, be gone.

lines.speaker: OLD MAN
lines.text: I’ll bring him the best ’parel that I have,

lines.speaker: OLD MAN
lines.text: Come on’t what will.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Sirrah naked fellow.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Poor Tom’s a-cold.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: I cannot daub it further.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Come hither, fellow.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: And yet I must. Bless thy sweet eyes, they bleed.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Know’st thou the way to Dover?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Both stile and gate, horseway and footpath. Poor Tom hath been

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: scared out of his good wits. Bless thee, good man’s son, from

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: the foul fiend! Five fiends have been in poor Tom at once; of

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: lust, as Obidicut; Hobbididence, prince of darkness; Mahu, of

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: stealing; Modo, of murder; Flibbertigibbet, of mopping and

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: mowing, who since possesses chambermaids and waiting women. So,

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: bless thee, master!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Here, take this purse, thou whom the heaven’s plagues

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Have humbled to all strokes: that I am wretched

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Makes thee the happier. Heavens deal so still!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Let the superfluous and lust-dieted man,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: That slaves your ordinance, that will not see

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Because he does not feel, feel your power quickly;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: So distribution should undo excess,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And each man have enough. Dost thou know Dover?

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Ay, master.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: There is a cliff, whose high and bending head

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Looks fearfully in the confined deep:

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Bring me but to the very brim of it,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And I’ll repair the misery thou dost bear

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: With something rich about me: from that place

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I shall no leading need.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Give me thy arm:

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Poor Tom shall lead thee.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Before the Duke of Albany’s Palace

lines.text: Enter Goneril, Edmund; Oswald meeting them.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Welcome, my lord. I marvel our mild husband

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Not met us on the way. Now, where’s your master?

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: Madam, within; but never man so chang’d.

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: I told him of the army that was landed;

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: He smil’d at it: I told him you were coming;

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: His answer was, ‘The worse.’ Of Gloucester’s treachery

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: And of the loyal service of his son

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: When I inform’d him, then he call’d me sot,

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: And told me I had turn’d the wrong side out.

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: What most he should dislike seems pleasant to him;

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: What like, offensive.
[_To Edmund._]

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Then shall you go no further.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: It is the cowish terror of his spirit,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: That dares not undertake. He’ll not feel wrongs

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Which tie him to an answer. Our wishes on the way

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: May prove effects. Back, Edmund, to my brother;

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Hasten his musters and conduct his powers.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: I must change names at home, and give the distaff

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Into my husband’s hands. This trusty servant

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Shall pass between us. Ere long you are like to hear,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: If you dare venture in your own behalf,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: A mistress’s command.
[_Giving a favour._]

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Wear this; spare speech;

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Decline your head. This kiss, if it durst speak,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Would stretch thy spirits up into the air.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Conceive, and fare thee well.

lines.speaker: EDMUND
lines.text: Yours in the ranks of death.
[_Exit Edmund._]

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: My most dear Gloucester.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: O, the difference of man and man!

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: To thee a woman’s services are due;

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: My fool usurps my body.

lines.speaker: OSWALD
lines.text: Madam, here comes my lord.
[_Exit._]
Enter Albany.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: I have been worth the whistle.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: O Goneril!

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: You are not worth the dust which the rude wind

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Blows in your face! I fear your disposition;

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: That nature which contemns its origin

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Cannot be bordered certain in itself.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: She that herself will sliver and disbranch

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: From her material sap, perforce must wither

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: And come to deadly use.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: No more; the text is foolish.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Wisdom and goodness to the vile seem vile;

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Filths savour but themselves. What have you done?

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Tigers, not daughters, what have you perform’d?

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: A father, and a gracious aged man,

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Whose reverence even the head-lugg’d bear would lick,

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Most barbarous, most degenerate, have you madded.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Could my good brother suffer you to do it?

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: A man, a prince, by him so benefitted!

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: If that the heavens do not their visible spirits

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Send quickly down to tame these vile offences,

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: It will come,

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Humanity must perforce prey on itself,

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Like monsters of the deep.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Milk-liver’d man!

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: That bear’st a cheek for blows, a head for wrongs;

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Who hast not in thy brows an eye discerning

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Thine honour from thy suffering; that not know’st

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Fools do those villains pity who are punish’d

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Ere they have done their mischief. Where’s thy drum?

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: France spreads his banners in our noiseless land;

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: With plumed helm thy state begins to threat,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Whilst thou, a moral fool, sitt’st still, and criest

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: ‘Alack, why does he so?’

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: See thyself, devil!

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Proper deformity seems not in the fiend

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: So horrid as in woman.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: O vain fool!

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Thou changed and self-cover’d thing, for shame!

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Be-monster not thy feature! Were’t my fitness

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: To let these hands obey my blood,

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: They are apt enough to dislocate and tear

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Thy flesh and bones. Howe’er thou art a fiend,

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: A woman’s shape doth shield thee.

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Marry, your manhood, mew!
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: What news?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: O, my good lord, the Duke of Cornwall’s dead;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Slain by his servant, going to put out

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The other eye of Gloucester.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Gloucester’s eyes!

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: A servant that he bred, thrill’d with remorse,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Oppos’d against the act, bending his sword

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: To his great master; who, thereat enrag’d,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Flew on him, and amongst them fell’d him dead;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: But not without that harmful stroke which since

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Hath pluck’d him after.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: This shows you are above,

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: You justicers, that these our nether crimes

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: So speedily can venge! But, O poor Gloucester!

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Lost he his other eye?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Both, both, my lord.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: This letter, madam, craves a speedy answer;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: ’Tis from your sister.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: One way I like this well;

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: But being widow, and my Gloucester with her,

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: May all the building in my fancy pluck

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: Upon my hateful life. Another way

lines.speaker: GONERIL
lines.text: The news is not so tart. I’ll read, and answer.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Where was his son when they did take his eyes?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Come with my lady hither.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: He is not here.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: No, my good lord; I met him back again.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Knows he the wickedness?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Ay, my good lord. ’Twas he inform’d against him;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And quit the house on purpose, that their punishment

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Might have the freer course.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Gloucester, I live

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: To thank thee for the love thou show’dst the King,

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: And to revenge thine eyes. Come hither, friend,

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Tell me what more thou know’st.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Kent and a Gentleman.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Why the King of France is so suddenly gone back, know you no

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: reason?

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Something he left imperfect in the state, which since his coming

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: forth is thought of, which imports to the kingdom so much fear

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: and danger that his personal return was most required and

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: necessary.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Who hath he left behind him general?

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: The Mareschal of France, Monsieur La Far.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Did your letters pierce the queen to any demonstration of grief?

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Ay, sir; she took them, read them in my presence;

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: And now and then an ample tear trill’d down

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Her delicate cheek. It seem’d she was a queen

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Over her passion; who, most rebel-like,

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Sought to be king o’er her.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: O, then it mov’d her.

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Not to a rage: patience and sorrow strove

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Who should express her goodliest. You have seen

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Sunshine and rain at once: her smiles and tears

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Were like a better day. Those happy smilets

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: That play’d on her ripe lip seem’d not to know

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: What guests were in her eyes; which parted thence

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: As pearls from diamonds dropp’d. In brief,

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Sorrow would be a rarity most belov’d,

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: If all could so become it.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Made she no verbal question?

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Faith, once or twice she heav’d the name of ‘father’

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Pantingly forth, as if it press’d her heart;

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Cried ‘Sisters, sisters! Shame of ladies! sisters!

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Kent! father! sisters! What, i’ the storm? i’ the night?

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Let pity not be believ’d!’ There she shook

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: The holy water from her heavenly eyes,

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: And clamour master’d her: then away she started

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: To deal with grief alone.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: It is the stars,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: The stars above us govern our conditions;

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Else one self mate and make could not beget

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Such different issues. You spoke not with her since?

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Was this before the King return’d?

lines.speaker: GENTLEMAN
lines.text: No, since.

lines.speaker: KENT

lines.text: Fall, and cease!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: This feather stirs; she lives! If it be so,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: It is a chance which does redeem all sorrows

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: That ever I have felt.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: O, my good master!
[_Kneeling._]

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Prythee, away!

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: ’Tis noble Kent, your friend.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: A plague upon you, murderers, traitors all!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I might have sav’d her; now she’s gone for ever!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Cordelia, Cordelia! stay a little. Ha!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: What is’t thou say’st? Her voice was ever soft,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Gentle, and low, an excellent thing in woman.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I kill’d the slave that was a-hanging thee.

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: ’Tis true, my lords, he did.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Did I not, fellow?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I have seen the day, with my good biting falchion

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I would have made them skip. I am old now,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: And these same crosses spoil me. Who are you?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Mine eyes are not o’ the best, I’ll tell you straight.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: If Fortune brag of two she lov’d and hated,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: One of them we behold.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: This is a dull sight. Are you not Kent?

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: The same,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Your servant Kent. Where is your servant Caius?

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: He’s a good fellow, I can tell you that;

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: He’ll strike, and quickly too:. He’s dead and rotten.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: No, my good lord; I am the very man.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: I’ll see that straight.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: That from your first of difference and decay

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Have follow’d your sad steps.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: You are welcome hither.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Nor no man else. All’s cheerless, dark and deadly.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Your eldest daughters have fordone themselves,

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: And desperately are dead.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Ay, so I think.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: He knows not what he says; and vain is it

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: That we present us to him.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Very bootless.
Enter an Officer.

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: Edmund is dead, my lord.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: That’s but a trifle here.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: You lords and noble friends, know our intent.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: What comfort to this great decay may come

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Shall be applied. For us, we will resign,

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: During the life of this old majesty,

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: To him our absolute power;
[_to Edgar and Kent_]

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: you to your rights;

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: With boot and such addition as your honours

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Have more than merited. All friends shall taste

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: The wages of their virtue and all foes

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: The cup of their deservings. O, see, see!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: And my poor fool is hang’d! No, no, no life!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Why should a dog, a horse, a rat have life,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: And thou no breath at all? Thou’lt come no more,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Never, never, never, never, never!

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Pray you undo this button. Thank you, sir.

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Do you see this? Look on her: look, her lips,

lines.speaker: LEAR
lines.text: Look there, look there!
[_He dies._]

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: He faints! My lord, my lord!

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Break, heart; I prythee break!

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Look up, my lord.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Vex not his ghost: O, let him pass! He hates him

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: That would upon the rack of this rough world

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: Stretch him out longer.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: He is gone indeed.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: The wonder is, he hath endur’d so long:

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: He but usurp’d his life.

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Bear them from hence. Our present business

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Is general woe. [_To Edgar and Kent._] Friends of my soul, you twain,

lines.speaker: ALBANY
lines.text: Rule in this realm and the gor’d state sustain.

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: I have a journey, sir, shortly to go;

lines.speaker: KENT
lines.text: My master calls me, I must not say no.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: The weight of this sad time we must obey;

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Speak what we feel, not what we ought to say.

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: The oldest hath borne most; we that are young

lines.speaker: EDGAR
lines.text: Shall never see so much, nor live so long.
[_Exeunt with a dead march._]
